task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: shot mix change from offensive substitutions
methodological_questions: Does a substitution that changes the offensive five detectably move shot mix (rim[path] share) beyond game-state and shooter effects?
What event-study or matched design is needed to separate personnel effects from coach-driven and game-state timing?
Can a placebo (e.g., defensive-only changes or dead-ball non-lineup changes) show the design does not manufacture shot-mix shifts?
Is the sample large enough, given that retrieved evidence shows sub-1pp mix shifts can be underpowered?

historical_evidence.finding: Related but different question: shot mix when the opposing rim big is off the floor. Recorded results: DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25, t=+3.3); POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18, t=+2.4); 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31, t=-5.8); rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4); PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007, t=+1.1). Run on N=1.07M possessions ([prior work]). Recorded verdict: WEAK/SMALL, will not carry a paper. Limited by [prior work]; risk RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

PULL_UP exposure-effect diagnostics. Slope with lineup fixed effects was -0.0255 (SE 0.0061); without lineup FE it was -0.0063 (SE 0.0036); the placebo on other play types was -0.0075 (SE 0.0017). Recorded verdict: artifact_found, attributed to shooter-level confounding. Limited by [prior work]; risks RISK:CONFOUNDING and RISK:PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE. Sample and power recorded as NOT_RECORDED.

Defensive in-game adaptation to repeated play type. League-wide within-game slope -0.0019 PPP per exposure (SE 0.0019); across-game +0.0004 (SE 0.0015). Only PULL_UP survived Holm correction (B -0.0243, SE 0.0061, holm 0.0004). Team-trait reliability was low (split-half r +0.008, season-to-season +0.037). Limited by [prior work], [prior work], and [prior work].

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a mix shift from a single lineup condition (opponent rim big off floor) using possession-level linear shifts.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as WEAK/SMALL with sub-1pp shifts and PPP t=+1.1. The rim-share effect was not distinguishable from zero (+0.12pp, SE 0.295 in [prior work]). Limited by small sample; RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER. Indicates that mix effects of this size need large samples and careful specification.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a PULL_UP shot-mix or exposure effect to a construct without controlling for shooter and lineup identity.
failed_approaches.why: The effect shrank by about 75% when lineup FE were removed, and a same-shooter placebo on other play types produced a similar slope. Recorded as an artifact from shooter-level confounding.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Estimating within-game adaptation to repeated play types from play-by-play labels.
failed_approaches.why: Estimates were near zero and the only survivor was PULL_UP. Recorded limitations were insufficient exposure, label or classification error, and low measurement reliability.

evidence_establishes: Prior work in this project (FAM:[prior work]) used the same data family and found that lineup-conditioned shot-mix shifts are detectable in large samples (N about 1.07M possessions) but small, with DRIVE and 3PA shifts of roughly 1-2pp.

Failure modes that recur in this project are shooter-level confounding ([prior work][prior work]), small effects with low power (FAM:[prior work]), and label or reliability problems (FAM:[prior work]). Any test of offensive-five effects must address these.
The retrieved records do not test the question as posed (offensive five change to shot mix). They are adjacent designs.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. No retrieved record estimates this directly from offensive substitutions.
Whether the design can detect personnel effects. A positive result would be a validation claim, and the retrieved records do not show that a validation design has been run.
The effect size of offensive-five changes, or whether it is larger than the opponent-big effect in FAM:[prior work].
Whether the 2022-23 to 2024-25 files support a clean event-study, since no record reports the number of offensive-five changes or their timing.
own_inferences: The question's premise is probably true in direction: offensive five changes that add or remove rim-oriented bigs or shooters should shift shot mix. The open question is whether the design isolates that from timing and matchup selection.
Offensive substitutions are endogenous. Coaches sub when they want a specific shot profile or matchup, so a naive pre/post comparison will overstate personnel effects.
The PULL_UP artifact ([prior work][prior work]) suggests that a shooter-fixed-effects design plus a placebo will be needed. Shooter identity is correlated with lineup membership.
Large possession counts may still give small standard errors on shot mix, so a sample-size argument should be made per lineup-pair, not per season.
uncertainties: Number of offensive-five change events per team-season and the distribution of time-on-floor per lineup are not recorded in the retrieval.
Shot-distance and shot-type reliability in the play-by-play is not documented in the retrieved records (LABEL_ERROR risk).
Whether [source]-database play-type records share the same lineup identification as the rotation intervals is unknown.
[prior work] (opener recommendations) was returned but is not about shot mix and was not relied on.

Whether the question is intended as a design-validation check (is the design sensitive enough?) or as a substantive effect estimate is not stated. The design below handles both, but the power target differs.

historical_effect.explanation: Without retrieved evidence, the default would be to run a simple pre/post comparison of shot mix around offensive substitutions. The retrieved records show that (a) shot-mix shifts of this size are small and were underpowered in FAM:[prior work], (b) lineup and shooter confounding produced an artifact in [prior work][prior work], and (c) label and reliability problems weakened FAM:[prior work]. These push the decision from a naive test to a proceed_with_changes design that uses a within-shooter event study, a placebo arm, and a pre-specified power calculation.

blocking_constraints.text: Shot-mix shifts of about 1-2pp (FAM:[prior work]) need large event counts. The number of offensive-five changes with sufficient floor time for each lineup pair must be checked before running.

Offensive substitutions are chosen by the coach in response to game state, fatigue, foul trouble, and matchups. [prior work][prior work] showed a shooter-level confound that shrank a lineup effect by about 75%.
The result is only credible if the design passes a placebo. [prior work][prior work] showed that a placebo can reproduce the apparent effect.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. FAM:[prior work] tests a related lineup-conditioned mix shift (opponent rim big off floor) and found small, unconvincing effects. [prior work][prior work] and FAM:[prior work] show confounding and reliability problems in adjacent exposure designs. Prior work partly informs the design but does not answer the question.

risks.text: Coach-driven substitution timing correlates with game state, matchup and shooter identity. Lineup effects can be shooter effects, as in [prior work][prior work].
Expected effects are small (sub-2pp, per FAM:[prior work]). Power per lineup pair may be low, and the design must be sized before analysis.
Shot distance and shot type come from play-by-play labels. Misclassification could bias rim and 3PA shares toward zero or distort the event study.
Team and lineup trait estimates have low reliability in FAM:[prior work], so lineup-level shot-mix measures may be noisy at the lineup-pair level.
A placebo on other play types or other personnel changes may fail to separate the offensive-five effect from defensive adaptation or shooter effects.
Some offensive lineups have few possessions, so shot-mix estimates for those lineups will be unstable.
Season-to-season changes in rules, pace and shot profile across 2022-23 to 2024-25 may confound pooled estimates.
Several shot categories (rim, drive, pull-up, post-up, 3PA) and several lineup pairs increase the chance of a spurious significant result, as in the multiple outcomes of FAM:[prior work].
Using end-of-stint or full-game stats to define the lineup or the pre-period could leak outcome information into the treatment definition.

design.estimand: Within-shooter, within-game change in shot-type shares (rim <=4ft, drive, pull-up, 3PA, post-up) for the offense when a substitution changes the offensive five, compared with matched pre-period baselines. Primary: the change in rim-plus-drive share. Secondary: 3PA share.
design.unit: Offensive stint (possession-level within a rotation interval), keyed to the team, the five-man lineup before and after the substitution, and the game.
design.sample: Regular season and playoffs, 2022-23 to 2024-25 (per the data description). Include only substitution events where the offensive five changes by at least two players, the new lineup has at least a pre-specified minimum number of possessions, and the substitution is not a dead-ball foul or timeout-driven change if those can be identified. Exact thresholds must be fixed before any run.
design.power: Compute before analysis using the observed count of qualifying events. Target: detect a 1pp change in rim-plus-drive share with 80% power at alpha 0.05 after clustering by game and team. If the power target is not met for a given lineup-pair class, report it as underpowered rather than as a null.
design.controls: Shooter fixed effects (to address [prior work][prior work]); game-state controls (score margin, period, time remaining); opponent-lineup controls; pre-period shot mix as the baseline; cluster-robust errors by game and team. Exclude shots taken in the first and last 2 minutes of each period to reduce timeout and foul-driven effects.
design.falsification: Placebo arms: (a) defensive-only personnel changes where the offensive five does not change; (b) offensive substitutions where the shooter who took the shot is not on the floor in the pre-period; (c) the same design applied to other play types (as in [prior work][prior work]). The design passes if the offensive-five effect is larger than the placebo effects and the placebo estimates are not significantly different from zero.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register one primary outcome (rim-plus-drive share). Apply Holm correction across secondary shot categories and lineup classes. Report the number of tests run.
design.decision_rule: Call the question supported if the primary effect is positive and significant after Holm correction, the shooter-FE estimate is within the CI of the shooter-free estimate, and the placebo arms show no comparable effect. Call it an artifact if the effect shrinks by more than half under shooter FE or if a placebo matches it. Call it rejected only if the design is powered for 1pp and the estimate is precisely zero. Otherwise report uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA regular season and playoffs 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25 per-game play-by-play, rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, and the derived play-type possession records. Freeze the data version and the lineup-identification code before analysis. Record the data version used at pre-registration (2026-11-02).
